title: AI delegation and professional judgment
text: Organizations increasingly delegate knowledge tasks to AI while retaining human responsibility for evaluation and accountability.

title: Relative performance and work intensification
text: When rewards depend on relative performance, productivity improvements can shift benchmarks and induce additional effort.

title: Exploration versus exploitation
text: Organizations balance search for new possibilities against refinement of familiar alternatives under resource constraints.

title: Attention as a scarce organizational resource
text: Decision makers allocate limited attention across competing tasks, creating bottlenecks when information production scales faster than review.

title: Scientific priority and racing
text: Research teams value priority and may trade deliberation for speed when competing groups pursue related discoveries.

title: Peer review as expert service capacity
text: Editorial systems depend on scarce expert review labor; increased submissions can generate congestion and weaker sorting.

title: Evaluation systems and measurable output
text: Performance metrics can redirect effort toward dimensions that are easier to count even when organizations ultimately value quality.

title: Knowledge diversity under common algorithms
text: Shared algorithmic tools can improve individual performance while also correlating search paths and narrowing collective diversity.

title: Resubmission and displaced workload
text: Rejected work often moves to another evaluation venue, shifting rather than eliminating screening and preparation costs.

title: Human verification of machine output
text: Machine-generated candidates can be abundant, but reliable decisions still require human checking, contextual judgment, and accountability.
